questions.question: What is the distance between a crest and a consecutive trough in a transverse wave?
questions.solution:
The distance between a crest and a consecutive trough is half of the wavelength.

 
• The highest surface part of a wave is called the crest, and the lowest part is the trough.
 
• The vertical distance between the crest and the trough is the wave height.
 
• The horizontal distance between two adjacent crests or troughs is known as the wavelength.

questions.question: Which among the following is **NOT** a Basic logical operator in Boolean Algebra laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NAND**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• All of the options listed are examples of logical operators that can be used in Boolean Algebra. However, among these options—AND, OR, NOT, and NAND—**the first three (AND, OR, NOT) **are usually referred to as the** basic or fundamental logical operators**. These are the operators from which all other logical operations can be derived.
 
• Therefore, **NAND **is **not considered a basic logical operator**. It's a **compound logical operator** that can be constructed from **AND **and **NOT** operators (it **essentially means "not AND"**).

questions.question: What is the mass of one mole of a substance in grams is called?
questions.solution:
• The **molar mass** of a substance is defined as the mass of 1 mol of that substance, expressed in grams per mole, and is equal to the mass of 6.022 × 10 23 atoms, molecules, or formula units of that substance.
 
• The **molecular mass (m)** is the mass of a given molecule: it is measured in daltons (Da or u). Different molecules of the same compound may have different molecular masses because they contain different isotopes of an element.
 
• **Atomic mass** is the number of protons and neutrons present in the atom, also called the mass number.

questions.question: How is the President of India elected?
questions.solution:
President of India is elected by “**single transferable vote**”.

 
• In this voting system, every member of “Electoral College” arranges the candidate's name in preference order.
 
• Votes are then counted and if after counting in round one no one emerges as a winner(to win the election one has to achieve more than 50% of the votes), then-candidate with least first preference votes is eliminated and then the second preference of those votes are counted and this process goes on until they get a clear winner.
 
• In this way the vote becomes transferable.
